{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-1)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{24}{7{x}^{4}}, & \,1\le x\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=-1]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-1)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|-1}=\frac{9}{7}.$

Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=-1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{24}{7{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{24}{7{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{24}{7}{[-\frac{1}{x}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{24}{7}[(-\frac{1}{2})-(-1)] \\  & =\frac{12}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=-1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=-1]-{\mu }_{X|-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{12}{7}-{(\frac{9}{7})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{12}{7}-\frac{81}{49} \\  & =\frac{3}{49}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,| \, X=x \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} y^2 \, f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, x) \: \textrm{d}y.
$$

Note that $\textrm E\big[ Y \,|\, X = x \big]$ is a function of $x.$ 

The conditional density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)} \\  & =2y,\end{aligned}
$$

where $1 \leq x \leq e, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.$ Outside this domain, we have $f_{Y|X} (y \,|\, x) = 0.$

Notice that $f_{Y|X} (y \,|\, x)$ does not depend on $x.$ Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot 2y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{y}^{3}\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=1] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=1]-{\mu }_{Y|1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{4}{9} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\textrm{Var}[X\,|\,Y] = \textrm{E}\big[(X - \mu_{X|y} \big)^2 \,|\, Y=y].
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2}\end{aligned}

$$

 

and $f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ Note that these formulas are analogous to those for $\textrm{Var}[X]$ for continuous $X.$

When we select a particular value of $y,$ the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ returns a real number. However, if $y$ is not specified, then $\textrm {Var}[X | Y = y]$ gives us a *function* of $y.$

- $f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$
